instruction: Your goal is to find information related to a specific patient’s lab tests. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10018845 and want to know all timestamps when the Hb value was 8 or lower during the patient’s last hospital visit. You want to search for Hb specifically, not other similar lab tests like "Hb C" or "Hb A2." When querying the DB agent, since you do not know how Hb is stored, use common terms like "Hb" or "Hgb" when referring to it, and let the DB agent find it for you.
gold_sql: WITH LastAdmission AS ( SELECT admissionid FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE patientid = 10018845 ORDER BY admitdatetime DESC LIMIT 1 ), HbTest AS ( SELECT itemcode FROM labtesttypes WHERE itemname = 'hemoglobin' ) SELECT lr.resultdatetime FROM labresults lr JOIN LastAdmission la ON lr.admissionid = la.admissionid JOIN HbTest ht ON lr.itemcode = ht.itemcode WHERE lr.patientid = 10018845 AND lr.resultvalue <= 8 AND lr.resultvalue IS NOT NULL ORDER BY lr.resultdatetime;

instruction: Your goal is to find the administration routes of specific ordered medications. Specifically, you are interested in the administration routes of ordered medications containing ISDN. instruction: Your goal is to find information about the prescription start time for a specific patient. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10004422 and you want to know the prescription start time for olanzapine and quetiapine prescribed simultaneously. gold_sql: WITH LastAdmission AS ( SELECT admissionid FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE patientid = 10004422 AND dischargedatetime IS NOT NULL ORDER BY admitdatetime DESC LIMIT 1 ), OlanzapinePrescriptions AS ( SELECT patientid, startdatetime FROM medicationorders WHERE admissionid IN (SELECT admissionid FROM LastAdmission) AND medicationname LIKE '%olanzapine%' ), QuetiapinePrescriptions AS ( SELECT patientid, startdatetime FROM medicationorders WHERE admissionid IN (SELECT admissionid FROM LastAdmission) AND medicationname LIKE '%quetiapine%' ) SELECT T1.startdatetime FROM OlanzapinePrescriptions T1 JOIN QuetiapinePrescriptions T2 ON T1.patientid = T2.patientid AND datetime(T1.startdatetime) = datetime(T2.startdatetime) AND T1.startdatetime = ( SELECT MIN(T1.startdatetime) FROM OlanzapinePrescriptions T1 JOIN QuetiapinePrescriptions T2 ON T1.patientid = T2.patientid AND datetime(T1.startdatetime) = datetime(T2.startdatetime) )

instruction: Your goal is to find information about a specific patient's lab tests. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10003400 and want to know the daily minimum Hb levels. You want to search for Hb specifically, but not other lab tests like "Hb C" or "Hb A2." instruction: Your goal is to find information related to patient diagnoses. gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT ha.admissionid FROM hospitaladmissions ha JOIN admissiondiagnoses ad ON ha.admissionid = ad.admissionid JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion WHERE ha.admitsource = 'emergency room' AND dc.description LIKE '%fracture%' ORDER BY ha.admissionid;

instruction: Your goal is to find the most frequently performed microbiological tests for patients who underwent a specific procedure. Specifically, you are interested in the procedure called percutaneous abdominal drainage, and you want to know which microbiological test was most commonly performed during the same hospital admission for these patients. You want to search for percutaneous abdominal drainage specifically, but not other similar procedures. When querying the DB agent, since you do not know how percutaneous abdominal drainage is stored, use common terms like "PAD" when referring to it, and let the DB agent find it for you. Since the database may record microbiological test times before procedure, you want to focus on microbiological tests conducted during the same hospital admission as the procedure. If multiple results tie for the highest frequency, you want to retrieve all of them. If a patient has multiple records of PAD across hospital admissions, you only want the first PAD record among them. If a patient has multiple records of the same microbiological test name, you want to count them only once per hospital admission.
gold_sql: WITH FirstPercAbdominalDrainage AS ( SELECT ap.patientid, ap.admissionid, ap.recordeddatetime AS first_drainage_time, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ap.patientid ORDER BY ap.recordeddatetime) AS rn FROM admissionprocedures ap JOIN procedurecodes pc ON ap.icdcode = pc.icdcode AND ap.codeversion = pc.codeversion WHERE pc.description = 'percutaneous abdominal drainage' ), FirstDrainagePatients AS ( SELECT patientid, admissionid FROM FirstPercAbdominalDrainage WHERE rn = 1 ), UniqueMicrobiologyTests AS ( SELECT DISTINCT mr.admissionid, mr.patientid, mr.testname FROM microbiologyresults mr JOIN FirstDrainagePatients fdp ON mr.admissionid = fdp.admissionid ), MicrobiologyTestCounts AS ( SELECT testname, COUNT(*) AS test_count, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rank FROM UniqueMicrobiologyTests GROUP BY testname ) SELECT testname FROM MicrobiologyTestCounts WHERE rank <= 1 ORDER BY rank;

instruction: Your goal is to find the number of patients admitted to the hospital who meet specific criteria. Specifically, you want to know how many patients admitted in the past 90 days have a family history of breast cancer.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ha.patientid) AS patient_count FROM hospitaladmissions ha JOIN admissiondiagnoses ad ON ha.admissionid = ad.admissionid JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion WHERE dc.description = 'family history of malignant neoplasm of breast' AND datetime(ha.admitdatetime) >= datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00', '-90 days')

instruction: Your goal is to find the length of a patient's hospital stay. Specifically, you want to know how many days patient ID 10000032 spent from admission to discharge. If this patient has multiple admission records, you want to know the average length of their stays in days.

instruction: Your goal is to find microbiology test information related to patients who underwent a specific procedure. Specifically, you want to know the top three most frequently collected specimen types from patients who underwent CVC placement, based on the same hospital admission record. Since the database may record microbiological test times before procedure, you want to focus on specimen types of microbiological tests conducted during the same hospital admission as the procedure. If multiple results tie for the same rank among the top frequent ranks, you want to retrieve all of them. If a patient has multiple records of CVC placement across hospital admissions, you only want the first CVC placement record among them. If a patient has multiple records of the microbiological test with the same specimen type, you want to count them only once per hospital admission.
gold_sql: WITH FirstCatheterPlacement AS (SELECT ap.patientid, ap.admissionid, ap.recordeddatetime AS first_catheter_time, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ap.patientid ORDER BY ap.recordeddatetime) AS rn FROM admissionprocedures ap JOIN procedurecodes pc ON ap.icdcode = pc.icdcode AND ap.codeversion = pc.codeversion WHERE pc.description LIKE '%central venous catheter%placement%'), FirstCatheterPatients AS (SELECT patientid, admissionid, first_catheter_time FROM FirstCatheterPlacement WHERE rn = 1), UniqueMicrobiologySpecimens AS (SELECT DISTINCT mr.admissionid, mr.patientid, mr.specimentype FROM microbiologyresults mr JOIN FirstCatheterPatients fcp ON mr.admissionid = fcp.admissionid), MicrobiologySpecCounts AS (SELECT specimentype, COUNT(*) AS spec_count, DENSE_RANK() OVER ( ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rank FROM UniqueMicrobiologySpecimens GROUP BY specimentype) SELECT specimentype FROM MicrobiologySpecCounts WHERE rank <= 3 ORDER BY rank;

instruction: Your goal is to identify medications prescribed to a patient following a specific surgery. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10016810 and want to know the medications with prescription start times recorded within the same hospital admission as their appendectomy. instruction: Your goal is to find the survival rate of patients diagnosed with a specific condition. Specifically, you want to know the percentage of patients diagnosed with septic shock who survive for at least 90 days. You want diagnosis names containing "septic shock." You want to assume the diagnosis time is the initial diagnosis time, and if a patient has no record of death 90 days after the diagnosis time, you want to consider them as having survived. You want the survival rate in percentage (%).
gold_sql: WITH SepticShockPatients AS ( SELECT ad.patientid, MIN(ad.recordeddatetime) AS first_diagnosis_time FROM admissiondiagnoses ad JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion WHERE dc.description LIKE '%septic shock%' GROUP BY ad.patientid ), SurvivalStatus AS ( SELECT ssp.patientid, ssp.first_diagnosis_time, d.dateofdeath, CASE WHEN d.dateofdeath IS NULL OR datetime(d.dateofdeath) >= datetime(ssp.first_diagnosis_time, '+90 days') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS survived FROM SepticShockPatients ssp JOIN demographics d ON ssp.patientid = d.patientid ) SELECT ROUND(100.0 * AVG(survived), 4) AS survival_rate_percentage FROM SurvivalStatus;

instruction: Your goal is to find the most common diagnoses for patients with specific conditions within a certain period. Specifically, you want to know the most frequent diagnosis names for patients with a BMI of 35 or higher from the same hospital admission record. You do not want to calculate BMI, but want to use information stored in the database. If multiple results tie for the highest frequency, you want to retrieve all of them. If a patient has multiple records of BMI (35 or higher) across hospital admissions, you only want the first BMI (35 or higher) record among them. If a patient has multiple records of the same diagnosis name, you want to count them only once per hospital admission.
gold_sql: WITH FirstBMIDiagnosis AS ( SELECT ad.patientid, ad.admissionid, ad.recordeddatetime AS first_bmi_time, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ad.patientid ORDER BY ad.recordeddatetime) AS rn FROM admissiondiagnoses ad JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion WHERE dc.description IN ( 'body mass index (bmi) 38.0-38.9, adult', 'body mass index (bmi) 35.0-35.9, adult', 'body mass index 35.0-35.9, adult', 'body mass index 40.0-44.9, adult' ) ), FirstBMIPatients AS ( SELECT patientid, admissionid FROM FirstBMIDiagnosis WHERE rn = 1 ), UniqueDiagnoses AS ( SELECT DISTINCT ad.admissionid, ad.patientid, dc.description FROM admissiondiagnoses ad JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion JOIN FirstBMIPatients fbp ON ad.admissionid = fbp.admissionid ), DiagnosisCounts AS ( SELECT description, COUNT(*) AS diagnosis_count, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rank FROM UniqueDiagnoses GROUP BY description ) SELECT description FROM DiagnosisCounts WHERE rank = 1 ORDER BY rank;

instruction: Your goal is to find how long it has been since a specific lab test was performed. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10004733 and want to know how many hours have passed since their last white blood cell test was conducted. gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(24 * (julianday('2100-12-31 23:59:00') - julianday(labresults.resultdatetime)), 4) FROM labresults WHERE labresults.itemcode IN ( SELECT labtesttypes.itemcode FROM labtesttypes WHERE labtesttypes.itemname IN ('wbc', 'white blood cells', 'wbc count', 'leukocytes') ) AND labresults.admissionid IN ( SELECT hospitaladmissions.admissionid FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE hospitaladmissions.patientid = 10004733 AND hospitaladmissions.dischargedatetime IS NULL ) ORDER BY labresults.resultdatetime DESC LIMIT 1;

instruction: Your goal is to find the cost of a specific ordered drug. Specifically, you want to know the cost of alteplase as recorded in the database. If there are multiple alteplase-related drugs, you want to know the cost of alteplase itself, not for catheter clearance use.

instruction: Your goal is to find microbiology test information related to patients with a specific diagnosis. Specifically, you are interested in patients diagnosed with severe sepsis and want to know the top three most frequently performed test names within the same hospital admission record. You want to search for diagnoses that include the word "severe sepsis" in their names. If multiple results tie for the same rank among the top frequent ranks, you want to retrieve all of them. If a patient has multiple records of severe sepsis across hospital admissions, you only want the first severe sepsis record among them. If a patient has multiple records of the same test name, you want to count them only once per hospital admission.
gold_sql: WITH SevereSepsisCodes AS ( SELECT icdcode, codeversion FROM diagnosiscodes WHERE description LIKE '%severe sepsis%' ), FirstSepsisDiagnosis AS ( SELECT a.patientid, a.admissionid, a.recordeddatetime AS first_recordeddatetime, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY a.patientid ORDER BY a.recordeddatetime) AS rn FROM admissiondiagnoses a JOIN SevereSepsisCodes s ON a.icdcode = s.icdcode AND a.codeversion = s.codeversion ), FirstSepsisPatients AS ( SELECT patientid, admissionid FROM FirstSepsisDiagnosis WHERE rn = 1 ), UniqueMicrobiologyTests AS ( SELECT DISTINCT m.admissionid, m.patientid, m.testname FROM microbiologyresults m JOIN FirstSepsisPatients f ON m.admissionid = f.admissionid WHERE m.testname IS NOT NULL ), MicrobiologyTestCounts AS ( SELECT testname, COUNT(*) AS test_count, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rank FROM UniqueMicrobiologyTests GROUP BY testname ) SELECT testname FROM MicrobiologyTestCounts WHERE rank <= 3 ORDER BY rank;

instruction: Your goal is to find the top five most frequently ordered medications alongside a specific drug. Specifically, you want to know which ordered medications have the same prescription start times with medications containing hydrocortisone most commonly. If multiple results tie for the same rank among the top frequent ranks, you want to retrieve all of them. You want medications containing hydrocortisone excluded from the final result.
gold_sql: WITH HydrocortisonePrescriptions AS ( SELECT mo.patientid, mo.admissionid, mo.startdatetime FROM medicationorders mo JOIN hospitaladmissions ha ON mo.admissionid = ha.admissionid WHERE mo.medicationname LIKE '%hydrocortisone%' ), OtherPrescriptions AS ( SELECT mo.patientid, mo.admissionid, mo.medicationname, mo.startdatetime FROM medicationorders mo JOIN hospitaladmissions ha ON mo.admissionid = ha.admissionid WHERE mo.medicationname NOT LIKE '%hydrocortisone%' ), CombinedPrescriptions AS ( SELECT o.medicationname AS drug, COUNT(*) AS prescription_count FROM HydrocortisonePrescriptions h JOIN OtherPrescriptions o ON h.patientid = o.patientid AND datetime(h.startdatetime) = datetime(o.startdatetime) GROUP BY o.medicationname ), RankedDrugs AS ( SELECT drug, prescription_count, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY prescription_count DESC) AS rank FROM CombinedPrescriptions ) SELECT drug FROM RankedDrugs WHERE rank <= 5 ORDER BY rank;

instruction: Your goal is to find the number of patients diagnosed with two specific conditions. Specifically, you want to know about patients diagnosed with cirrhosis. You want diagnosis names containing "cirrhosis." Among those patients, you want to know how many also received a diagnosis of hepatic encephalopathy in the same hospital admission record.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT lc.patientid) AS patient_count FROM (SELECT ad.patientid, ad.admissionid FROM admissiondiagnoses ad JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion WHERE dc.description LIKE '%cirrhosis%' ) lc JOIN (SELECT ad.patientid, ad.admissionid FROM admissiondiagnoses ad JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion WHERE dc.description = 'hepatic encephalopathy') he ON lc.admissionid = he.admissionid;

instruction: Your goal is to find information related to the seasonality of a specific diagnosis. Specifically, you want to know which month has the highest number of asthma diagnosis cases. If there are multiple months with the same highest rank, you want all of them reported. You want the output formatted as a two-digit string (e.g., '01').
gold_sql: WITH asthma_diagnoses AS ( SELECT ad.patientid, ad.admissionid, ad.recordeddatetime FROM admissiondiagnoses ad JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion WHERE dc.description IN ('asthma, unspecified type, unspecified', 'unspecified asthma, uncomplicated') ), monthly_counts AS ( SELECT strftime('%m', recordeddatetime) AS diagnosis_month, COUNT(DISTINCT patientid || '-' || admissionid) AS case_count FROM asthma_diagnoses WHERE recordeddatetime IS NOT NULL GROUP BY diagnosis_month ) SELECT diagnosis_month FROM monthly_counts WHERE case_count = (SELECT MAX(case_count) FROM monthly_counts);

instruction: Your goal is to find the mortality rates associated with specific treatments for elderly patients. Specifically, you want to identify the treatment with the highest mortality rate among patients aged 65 and older who underwent surgery, focusing on deaths occurring within 30 days post-surgery. If multiple results tie for the highest frequency, you want to retrieve all of them. You want to treat multiple instances of the same procedure for the same patient as independent cases for the calculation. If the database contains age information at the time of admission, you want to use that information directly rather than calculating the age.
gold_sql: WITH ElderlyPatients AS ( SELECT d.patientid, d.dateofdeath FROM demographics d JOIN hospitaladmissions ha ON d.patientid = ha.patientid WHERE ha.age >= 65 ), ProcedureEvents AS ( SELECT ap.patientid, ap.admissionid, ap.recordeddatetime AS procedure_time, pc.description AS procedure_name FROM admissionprocedures ap JOIN procedurecodes pc ON ap.icdcode = pc.icdcode AND ap.codeversion = pc.codeversion JOIN ElderlyPatients ep ON ap.patientid = ep.patientid ) SELECT procedure_name FROM ( SELECT pe.procedure_name, SUM(CASE WHEN ep.dateofdeath IS NOT NULL AND datetime(ep.dateofdeath) BETWEEN datetime(pe.procedure_time) AND datetime(pe.procedure_time, '+30 days') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(h.patientid) AS mortality_rate, DENSE_RANK() OVER ( ORDER BY SUM(CASE WHEN ep.dateofdeath IS NOT NULL AND datetime(ep.dateofdeath) BETWEEN datetime(pe.procedure_time) AND datetime(pe.procedure_time, '+30 days') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(h.patientid) DESC ) AS rank FROM ProcedureEvents pe JOIN hospitaladmissions h ON pe.admissionid = h.admissionid JOIN ElderlyPatients ep ON pe.patientid = ep.patientid GROUP BY pe.procedure_name ) subquery WHERE rank <= 1 ORDER BY mortality_rate DESC;

instruction: Your goal is to find which procedures were conducted for patients at or after the time of a specific diagnosis. Specifically, you want to know the top five most frequently performed procedures within 6 hours of a hospital admission during which patients received atrial fibrillation. You want to search for various types of atrial fibrillation, but not atrial flutter or similar conditions. If multiple results tie for the same rank among the top frequent ranks, you want to retrieve all of them. If a patient has multiple records of atrial fibrillation across hospital admissions, you only want the first atrial fibrillation record among them. gold_sql: WITH FirstAFDiagnosis AS ( SELECT ad.patientid, ad.admissionid, ad.recordeddatetime AS first_af_time, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ad.patientid ORDER BY ad.recordeddatetime) AS rn FROM admissiondiagnoses ad JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion WHERE LOWER(dc.description) LIKE '%atrial fibrillation%' ), FirstAFStay AS ( SELECT patientid, admissionid, first_af_time FROM FirstAFDiagnosis WHERE rn = 1 ), UniqueProcedures AS ( SELECT DISTINCT ap.admissionid, ap.patientid, pc.description AS procedure_name FROM FirstAFStay f JOIN admissionprocedures ap ON ap.admissionid = f.admissionid JOIN procedurecodes pc ON ap.icdcode = pc.icdcode AND ap.codeversion = pc.codeversion WHERE ap.recordeddatetime IS NOT NULL AND f.first_af_time IS NOT NULL AND datetime(ap.recordeddatetime) BETWEEN datetime(f.first_af_time) AND datetime(f.first_af_time, '+6 hours') ), ProcedureCounts AS ( SELECT procedure_name, COUNT(*) AS procedure_count, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rank FROM UniqueProcedures GROUP BY procedure_name ) SELECT procedure_name FROM ProcedureCounts WHERE rank <= 5 ORDER BY rank;

instruction: Your goal is to find the duration of hospital stays for patients. Specifically, you want to know the patient with the longest hospital stay. You also want to include currently admitted patients in the results. If multiple results tie for the highest frequency, you want to retrieve all of them.
gold_sql: WITH stay_duration AS ( SELECT d.patientid, ha.admissionid, ha.admitdatetime, ha.dischargedatetime, CASE WHEN ha.dischargedatetime IS NULL THEN JULIANDAY('2100-12-31 23:59:00') - JULIANDAY(ha.admitdatetime) ELSE JULIANDAY(ha.dischargedatetime) - JULIANDAY(ha.admitdatetime) END AS duration_days FROM demographics d JOIN hospitaladmissions ha ON d.patientid = ha.patientid ), ranked_stays AS ( SELECT patientid, admissionid, admitdatetime, dischargedatetime, ROUND(duration_days, 4) AS duration_days, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY duration_days DESC) AS rank FROM stay_duration ) SELECT patientid FROM ranked_stays WHERE rank = 1;

instruction: Your goal is to find information related to care units. Specifically, you want to identify the hospital care unit with the highest number of transfers in the past 180 days. gold_sql: WITH RankedCareUnits AS ( SELECT pt.careunit, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) as rank FROM patienttransfers pt WHERE pt.careunit IS NOT NULL AND transfertype = 'transfer' AND datetime(pt.transferindatetime) >= datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00','-180 days') GROUP BY pt.careunit ) SELECT careunit FROM RankedCareUnits WHERE rank = 1;

instruction: Your goal is to find out how much time has elapsed since a specific medication was prescribed to a patient. instruction: Your goal is to find all the care units a patient was transferred to during their hospital stay.
