instruction: Your goal is to find the most frequently prescribed medications for a specific patient group. Specifically, you want to identify the top three medications most commonly prescribed to patients aged 60 or older after a COPD diagnosis. When searching for COPD, you want to use the keywords 'chronic obstructive pulmonary', 'obstructive chronic bronchitis', and 'chronic airway obstruction' to identify diagnosis names that include these terms. You want to limit the medication prescriptions to those recorded after the COPD diagnosis within the same hospital admission, based on their prescription start time. If multiple results tie for the same rank among the top frequent ranks, you want to retrieve all of them. If a patient has multiple records of COPD across hospital admissions, you only want the first COPD record among them. If a patient has multiple records of the same medication name, you want to count them only once per hospital admission. If the database contains age information at the time of admission, you want to use that information directly rather than calculating the age.
gold_sql: WITH FirstCOPDDiagnosis AS ( SELECT ad.patientid, ad.admissionid, ad.recordeddatetime AS first_copd_time, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ad.patientid ORDER BY ad.recordeddatetime) AS rn FROM admissiondiagnoses ad JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion JOIN hospitaladmissions ha ON ad.admissionid = ha.admissionid WHERE (dc.description LIKE '%chronic obstructive pulmonary%' OR dc.description LIKE '%obstructive chronic bronchitis%' OR dc.description LIKE '%chronic airway obstruction%') AND ha.age >= 60 ), FirstAdmission AS ( SELECT patientid, admissionid, first_copd_time FROM FirstCOPDDiagnosis WHERE rn = 1 ), UniquePrescriptions AS ( SELECT DISTINCT mo.admissionid, mo.patientid, mo.medicationname FROM medicationorders mo JOIN FirstAdmission fa ON mo.admissionid = fa.admissionid WHERE mo.startdatetime >= fa.first_copd_time ), DrugCounts AS ( SELECT medicationname, COUNT(*) AS prescription_count, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rank FROM UniquePrescriptions GROUP BY medicationname ) SELECT medicationname FROM DrugCounts WHERE rank <= 3 ORDER BY rank;

instruction: Your goal is to find the number of patients who received a specific diagnosis and subsequently underwent a specific surgery or procedure. Specifically, you want to know how many unique patients diagnosed with breast cancer underwent a mastectomy during the same hospital admission.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.patientid) FROM ( SELECT ha.patientid, ad.recordeddatetime AS charttime, ha.admissionid FROM admissiondiagnoses ad JOIN hospitaladmissions ha ON ad.admissionid = ha.admissionid JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion WHERE (dc.description = 'malignant neoplasm of central portion of female breast') ) AS T1 JOIN ( SELECT ha.patientid, ap.recordeddatetime AS charttime, ha.admissionid FROM admissionprocedures ap JOIN hospitaladmissions ha ON ap.admissionid = ha.admissionid JOIN procedurecodes pc ON ap.icdcode = pc.icdcode AND ap.codeversion = pc.codeversion WHERE (pc.description = 'unilateral simple mastectomy') ) AS T2 ON T1.patientid = T2.patientid WHERE T1.charttime < T2.charttime AND T1.admissionid = T2.admissionid;

instruction: Your goal is to find information about drug prescriptions. Specifically, you want to know the top 5 most frequently prescribed drugs. If multiple results tie for the same rank among the top frequent ranks, you want to retrieve all of them. If there is at least one result, you want to narrow the results to prescriptions starting this month.
gold_sql: WITH PrescriptionCounts AS ( SELECT medicationname AS drug, COUNT(*) AS prescription_count FROM medicationorders WHERE datetime(startdatetime, 'start of month') = datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00', 'start of month') GROUP BY medicationname ), RankedDrugs AS ( SELECT drug, prescription_count, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY prescription_count DESC) AS rank FROM PrescriptionCounts ) SELECT drug FROM RankedDrugs WHERE rank <= 5 ORDER BY rank;

instruction: Your goal is to find the cost of a specific procedure stored in the database. Specifically, you want to know the cost of laparoscopic robot-assisted procedure.
gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT costrecords.costamount FROM costrecords WHERE costrecords.eventtype = 'admissionprocedures' AND costrecords.costid IN ( SELECT admissionprocedures.recordid FROM admissionprocedures WHERE (admissionprocedures.icdcode, admissionprocedures.codeversion) IN ( SELECT procedurecodes.icdcode, procedurecodes.codeversion FROM procedurecodes WHERE procedurecodes.description = 'laparoscopic robotic assisted procedure' ) )

instruction: Your goal is to find the specific lab test values for a patient following a particular diagnosis. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10037861 and want to know the highest NT-proBNP value measured during the same hospital admission after a heart failure diagnosis.
gold_sql: WITH heart_failure_diagnosis AS ( SELECT ad.patientid, ad.admissionid, ad.recordeddatetime AS diag_time FROM admissiondiagnoses ad JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion WHERE ad.patientid = 10037861 AND lower(dc.description) LIKE '%heart failure%' ), ntprobnp_item AS ( SELECT itemcode FROM labtesttypes WHERE lower(itemname) LIKE 'ntprobnp' ) SELECT MAX(lr.resultvalue) AS max_ntprobnp FROM labresults lr JOIN heart_failure_diagnosis hfd ON lr.patientid = hfd.patientid AND lr.admissionid = hfd.admissionid AND lr.resultdatetime >= hfd.diag_time JOIN ntprobnp_item ni ON lr.itemcode = ni.itemcode WHERE lr.resultvalue IS NOT NULL;

instruction: Your goal is to find cost-related information for patients with a specific diagnosis. Specifically, you want to know the total costs incurred during the same hospital admission for patients diagnosed with end-stage or stage 5 renal disease. If a patient received the same diagnosis name multiple times, you want to include only the hospital admission associated with the first diagnosis in the results.
gold_sql: WITH FirstESRDDiagnosis AS ( SELECT ad.patientid, ad.admissionid, ad.recordeddatetime AS first_esrd_time, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ad.patientid ORDER BY ad.recordeddatetime) AS rn FROM admissiondiagnoses ad JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion WHERE dc.description = 'end stage renal disease' OR dc.description LIKE '%stage 5 chronic kidney disease%' OR dc.description LIKE '%chronic kidney disease stage v%' ), FirstAdmission AS ( SELECT patientid, admissionid FROM FirstESRDDiagnosis WHERE rn = 1 ), AdmissionCosts AS ( SELECT fa.patientid, SUM(cr.costamount) AS total_cost FROM FirstAdmission fa JOIN hospitaladmissions ha ON fa.admissionid = ha.admissionid JOIN costrecords cr ON fa.admissionid = cr.admissionid GROUP BY fa.patientid ) SELECT ROUND(AVG(total_cost), 4) AS average_cost FROM AdmissionCosts;

instruction: Your goal is to find information about a specific patient's I/O. Specifically, you want to know the Net I/O for patient ID 10018081 for today. You want the final value to be the total input amount minus the output amount for today.
gold_sql: WITH InputTotal AS ( SELECT COALESCE(SUM(totalvolume), 0) AS total_input FROM intakerecords WHERE patientid = 10018081 AND datetime(startdatetime, 'start of day') = datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00', 'start of day') ), OutputTotal AS ( SELECT COALESCE(SUM(volume), 0) AS total_output FROM outputrecords WHERE patientid = 10018081 AND datetime(recordeddatetime, 'start of day') = datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00', 'start of day') ) SELECT (SELECT total_input FROM InputTotal) - (SELECT total_output FROM OutputTotal) AS net_io;

instruction: Your goal is to find the number of patients from whom a specific type of microbiology specimen was collected. Specifically, you want to know how many unique patients had cerebrospinal fluid specimens collected. After retrieving the results, you want to narrow the result to the last 180 days.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT hospitaladmissions.patientid) FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE hospitaladmissions.admissionid IN ( SELECT microbiologyresults.admissionid FROM microbiologyresults WHERE microbiologyresults.specimentype = 'csf;spinal fluid' AND datetime(microbiologyresults.collecteddatetime) >= datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00', '-180 days') );

instruction: Your goal is to find cost-related information for patients with a specific diagnosis. Specifically, you want to know the average total cost incurred during the same hospital admission for patients who underwent CVC placement. If a patient received the same procedure name multiple times, you want to include only the hospital admission associated with the first instance of that procedure in the results.
gold_sql: WITH FirstCatheterPlacement AS ( SELECT ap.patientid, ap.admissionid, ap.recordeddatetime AS first_placement_time, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ap.patientid ORDER BY ap.recordeddatetime) AS rn FROM admissionprocedures ap JOIN procedurecodes pc ON ap.icdcode = pc.icdcode AND ap.codeversion = pc.codeversion WHERE pc.description LIKE '%central venous catheter%placement%' ), FirstPlacementAdmissions AS ( SELECT patientid, admissionid FROM FirstCatheterPlacement WHERE rn = 1 ), AdmissionCosts AS ( SELECT f.patientid, f.admissionid, SUM(cr.costamount) AS total_cost FROM FirstPlacementAdmissions f JOIN costrecords cr ON cr.admissionid = f.admissionid GROUP BY f.admissionid ) SELECT ROUND(AVG(total_cost), 4) AS average_cost FROM AdmissionCosts;

instruction: Your goal is to find the number of times a specific lab test was performed for a patient. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10004235 and you want to know how many lactate measurement records exist within 48 hours following the first severe sepsis diagnosis. You want to search for diagnoses that include the word "severe sepsis" in their names.
gold_sql: WITH FirstSevereSepsis AS ( SELECT ad.patientid, ad.admissionid, ad.recordeddatetime AS first_sepsis_time, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ad.patientid ORDER BY ad.recordeddatetime) AS rn FROM admissiondiagnoses ad JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion WHERE dc.description LIKE '%severe sepsis%' AND ad.patientid = 10004235 ), FirstSepsisDiagnosis AS ( SELECT patientid, admissionid, first_sepsis_time FROM FirstSevereSepsis WHERE rn = 1 ), LactateMeasurements AS ( SELECT lr.patientid, lr.resultdatetime FROM labresults lr JOIN labtesttypes lt ON lr.itemcode = lt.itemcode JOIN FirstSepsisDiagnosis fsd ON lr.patientid = fsd.patientid WHERE lt.itemname = 'lactate' AND datetime(lr.resultdatetime) BETWEEN datetime(fsd.first_sepsis_time) AND datetime(fsd.first_sepsis_time, '+48 hours') ) SELECT COUNT(*) AS lactate_measurement_count FROM LactateMeasurements;

instruction: Your goal is to find if a specific patient's respiratory rate in the ICU is below a certain level. Specifically, you are interested in respiratory rates measured yesterday and today, and you want to check if any measurements were recorded as 12 or lower. If such records exist, ask to provide the list of such patients.
gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT d.patientid FROM clinicalevents ce JOIN icuepisodes ie ON ce.admissionid = ie.admissionid AND ce.icuadmissionid = ie.icuadmissionid JOIN demographics d ON ce.patientid = d.patientid JOIN clinicalitemtypes cit ON ce.itemcode = cit.itemcode WHERE cit.itemname = 'respiratory rate' AND ce.value <= 12 AND (datetime(ce.recordeddatetime, 'start of day') = datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00', 'start of day', '-1 day') OR (datetime(ce.recordeddatetime, 'start of day') = datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00', 'start of day', '0 day')));

instruction: Your goal is to find one body measurement for a currently admitted patient. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10021487 and you want to know the patient’s height.
gold_sql: SELECT clinicalevents.value FROM clinicalevents WHERE clinicalevents.icuadmissionid IN ( SELECT icuepisodes.icuadmissionid FROM icuepisodes WHERE icuepisodes.admissionid IN ( SELECT hospitaladmissions.admissionid FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE hospitaladmissions.patientid = 10021487 ) ) AND clinicalevents.itemcode IN ( SELECT clinicalitemtypes.itemcode FROM clinicalitemtypes WHERE clinicalitemtypes.itemname = 'height (cm)' AND clinicalitemtypes.itemtype = 'clinicalevents' ) ORDER BY clinicalevents.recordeddatetime DESC LIMIT 1;

instruction: Your goal is to find the number of patients who underwent specific procedures. Specifically, you want to know how many patients received both a colonoscopy and an EGD during the same hospital admission.
gold_sql: WITH ColonoscopyPatients AS ( SELECT p.patientid, p.admissionid FROM admissionprocedures p JOIN procedurecodes d ON p.icdcode = d.icdcode AND p.codeversion = d.codeversion WHERE d.description = 'colonoscopy' ), EGDPatients AS ( SELECT p.patientid, p.admissionid FROM admissionprocedures p JOIN procedurecodes d ON p.icdcode = d.icdcode AND p.codeversion = d.codeversion WHERE d.description = 'esophagogastroduodenoscopy [egd] with closed biopsy' ) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.patientid) AS patient_count FROM ColonoscopyPatients c JOIN EGDPatients e ON c.patientid = e.patientid AND c.admissionid = e.admissionid;

instruction: Your goal is to find the duration of ICU stays for a specific patient. You are interested in patient ID 10016742 and you want to know the average number of days the patient spent in the ICU per hospital visit. If a hospital visit includes multiple ICU stays, you want to sum them for the calculation.
gold_sql: WITH icu_duration AS ( SELECT admissionid, SUM(julianday(dischargedatetime) - julianday(admitdatetime)) AS total_icu_days FROM icuepisodes WHERE patientid = 10016742 AND dischargedatetime IS NOT NULL GROUP BY admissionid ) SELECT ROUND(AVG(total_icu_days), 4) AS avg_icu_days_per_admission FROM icu_duration;

instruction: Your goal is to find information about a patient's specific vital signs. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10018081 and you want to know the time of the lowest heart rate recorded yesterday. If there are multiple instances of the lowest value, you want to know all corresponding times.
gold_sql: WITH HeartRateItem AS ( SELECT itemcode FROM clinicalitemtypes WHERE itemname = 'heart rate' LIMIT 1 ), MinHeartRate AS ( SELECT MIN(c.value) AS min_hr FROM clinicalevents c JOIN HeartRateItem hri ON c.itemcode = hri.itemcode WHERE c.patientid = 10018081 AND datetime(c.recordeddatetime, 'start of day') = datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00', 'start of day', '-1 day') ) SELECT c.recordeddatetime FROM clinicalevents c JOIN HeartRateItem hri ON c.itemcode = hri.itemcode WHERE c.patientid = 10018081 AND datetime(c.recordeddatetime, 'start of day') = datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00', 'start of day', '-1 day') AND c.value = (SELECT min_hr FROM MinHeartRate) AND c.value IS NOT NULL ORDER BY c.recordeddatetime;

instruction: Your goal is to find information about a specific patient. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10038992 and you want to know the patient’s age at the most recent hospital admission. If the database contains age information at the time of admission, you want to use that information directly rather than calculating the age.
gold_sql: SELECT age FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE patientid = 10038992 ORDER BY admitdatetime DESC LIMIT 1;

instruction: Your goal is to find the lab test results for a specific patient. You are interested in patient ID 10008287 and you want to know the platelet values recorded during their most recent hospital admission.
gold_sql: WITH latest_admission AS ( SELECT admissionid FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE patientid = 10008287 ORDER BY admitdatetime DESC LIMIT 1 ) SELECT lr.resultvalue FROM labresults lr JOIN labtesttypes ltt ON lr.itemcode = ltt.itemcode WHERE lr.admissionid = (SELECT admissionid FROM latest_admission) AND ltt.itemname = 'platelet count';

instruction: Your goal is to find information about a specific patient's prescription. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10025463, and you want to know the first prescription start time for oxycodone for the patient in November of this year.
gold_sql: SELECT startdatetime FROM medicationorders WHERE patientid = 10025463 AND medicationname LIKE '%oxycodone%' AND strftime('%Y-%m', startdatetime) = '2100-11' ORDER BY startdatetime ASC LIMIT 1;

instruction: Your goal is to find the survival rate of patients who received a specific drug after a particular treatment. Specifically, you want to know the average survival rate of patients diagnosed with multiple myeloma and prescribed lenalidomide. You want to assume the diagnosis time as the initial diagnosis date and the drug prescription time as the start of the prescription. If a patient has no death record within one year from the diagnosis date, you want to consider them as having survived. You want to search for diagnoses that include the word "multiple myeloma" in their names. You want the survival rate in percentage (%).
gold_sql: WITH MultipleMyelomaPatients AS ( SELECT ad.patientid, MIN(ad.recordeddatetime) AS first_diagnosis_time FROM admissiondiagnoses ad JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion WHERE dc.description LIKE '%multiple myeloma%' GROUP BY ad.patientid ), LenalidomidePatients AS ( SELECT mmp.patientid, mmp.first_diagnosis_time FROM MultipleMyelomaPatients mmp JOIN medicationorders mo ON mmp.patientid = mo.patientid WHERE mo.medicationname LIKE '%lenalidomide%' AND datetime(mo.startdatetime) >= datetime(mmp.first_diagnosis_time) ), SurvivalStatus AS ( SELECT lp.patientid, lp.first_diagnosis_time, d.dateofdeath, CASE WHEN d.dateofdeath IS NULL OR datetime(d.dateofdeath) > datetime(lp.first_diagnosis_time, '+1 year') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS survived FROM LenalidomidePatients lp JOIN demographics d ON lp.patientid = d.patientid ) SELECT 100.0 * AVG(survived) AS survival_rate_percentage FROM SurvivalStatus;

instruction: Your goal is to find information related to patient admissions. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10004422 and you want to know the admission type for their most recent hospital visit.
gold_sql: SELECT hospitaladmissions.admissiontype FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE hospitaladmissions.patientid = 10004422 AND hospitaladmissions.dischargedatetime IS NOT NULL ORDER BY hospitaladmissions.admitdatetime DESC LIMIT 1;

instruction: Your goal is to find cost-related information for patients meeting specific lab value conditions. Specifically, you want to know the average total cost of hospital admissions for patients with creatinine levels exceeding 5. If a patient has multiple instances of creatinine levels above 5, you want to include only the first such hospital admission in the results. You specifically want the creatinine level, not urinary creatinine.
gold_sql: WITH FirstHighCreatinine AS ( SELECT lr.patientid, lr.admissionid, lr.resultdatetime AS first_high_time, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY lr.patientid ORDER BY lr.resultdatetime) AS rn FROM labresults lr JOIN labtesttypes ltt ON lr.itemcode = ltt.itemcode WHERE ltt.itemname = 'creatinine' AND lr.resultvalue > 5.0 ), FirstCreatinineAdmissions AS ( SELECT patientid, admissionid FROM FirstHighCreatinine WHERE rn = 1 ), AdmissionCosts AS ( SELECT f.patientid, f.admissionid, SUM(cr.costamount) AS total_cost FROM FirstCreatinineAdmissions f JOIN costrecords cr ON cr.admissionid = f.admissionid GROUP BY f.admissionid ) SELECT ROUND(AVG(total_cost), 4) AS average_cost FROM AdmissionCosts;

instruction: Your goal is to find if a patient's SpO2 deviated from the normal range during a specific month. Specifically, you want to check if there are any records this month where SpO2 was below 90% or above 100%. If such records exist, ask to retrieve how many patients were in that condition.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ce.patientid) AS patient_count FROM clinicalevents ce JOIN clinicalitemtypes cit ON ce.itemcode = cit.itemcode JOIN hospitaladmissions ha ON ce.admissionid = ha.admissionid WHERE cit.itemname = 'o2 saturation pulseoxymetry' AND ce.value IS NOT NULL AND (ce.value < 90 OR ce.value > 100) AND datetime(ce.recordeddatetime, 'start of month') = datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00', 'start of month')

instruction: Your goal is to find the vital information of a specific patient. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10004733 and you want to know the daily average respiratory rate during the current hospital visit. You want to see the results for yesterday and today.
gold_sql: WITH RespiratoryItem AS ( SELECT itemcode FROM clinicalitemtypes WHERE itemname = 'respiratory rate' LIMIT 1 ), CurrentAdmissions AS ( SELECT admissionid FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE patientid = 10004733 AND dischargedatetime IS NULL ) SELECT ROUND(AVG(ce.value), 4) AS avg_respiratory_rate FROM clinicalevents ce JOIN RespiratoryItem ri ON ce.itemcode = ri.itemcode JOIN CurrentAdmissions ca ON ce.admissionid = ca.admissionid WHERE ce.patientid = 10004733 AND (datetime(ce.recordeddatetime, 'start of day') = datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00', 'start of day', '-1 day') OR datetime(ce.recordeddatetime, 'start of day') = datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00', 'start of day')) AND ce.value IS NOT NULL GROUP BY date(ce.recordeddatetime) ORDER BY date(ce.recordeddatetime);

instruction: Your goal is to find the most frequently performed tests for a patient group. Specifically, you want to know the top five lab tests conducted on patients aged 65 and older. If multiple results tie for the same rank among the top frequent ranks, you want to retrieve all of them. If a patient has multiple records of the same lab test name, you want to count them only once per patient. If the database contains age information at the time of admission, you want to use that information directly rather than calculating the age.
gold_sql: WITH UniqueLabTests AS ( SELECT DISTINCT l.patientid, l.itemcode, t.itemname FROM labresults l JOIN hospitaladmissions h ON l.admissionid = h.admissionid JOIN labtesttypes t ON l.itemcode = t.itemcode WHERE h.age >= 65 ), TestCounts AS ( SELECT itemname, COUNT(DISTINCT patientid) as patient_count, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT patientid) DESC) as rank FROM UniqueLabTests GROUP BY itemname ) SELECT itemname FROM TestCounts WHERE rank <= 5 ORDER BY rank;

instruction: Your goal is to find information about a patient’s output record. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10009035, and you want to know the total urine output measured in the 4 hours following the first phenylephrine administration during their last hospital visit. You want to identify urine output using the item names 'foley' and 'or urine'. You want the phenylephrine data from patient input records, not prescription records.
gold_sql: WITH LastAdmission AS ( SELECT admissionid, admitdatetime FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE patientid = 10009035 ORDER BY admitdatetime DESC LIMIT 1 ), FirstPhenylephrine AS ( SELECT MIN(ir.startdatetime) AS phenylephrine_start FROM intakerecords ir JOIN LastAdmission la ON ir.admissionid = la.admissionid JOIN clinicalitemtypes cit ON ir.itemcode = cit.itemcode WHERE ir.patientid = 10009035 AND cit.itemname LIKE '%phenylephrine%' ), TotalUrineOutput AS ( SELECT SUM(o.volume) AS total_urine_output FROM outputrecords o JOIN LastAdmission la ON o.admissionid = la.admissionid JOIN FirstPhenylephrine fp ON o.recordeddatetime >= fp.phenylephrine_start AND o.recordeddatetime <= datetime(fp.phenylephrine_start, '+4 hours') JOIN clinicalitemtypes cit ON o.itemcode = cit.itemcode WHERE o.patientid = 10009035 AND (cit.itemname = 'foley' OR cit.itemname = 'or urine') ) SELECT total_urine_output FROM TotalUrineOutput;

instruction: Your goal is to find the medications used by patients with a specific diagnosis. Specifically, you are interested in patients in their 40s and 50s, and you want to know the top five ordered medications within the same hospital record as a depressive disorder diagnosis. You want the diagnosis names that include the word "depressive disorder." If multiple results tie for the same rank among the top frequent ranks, you want to retrieve all of them. If a patient has multiple records of depressive disorder across hospital admissions, you only want the first depressive disorder record among them. If a patient has multiple records of the same medication name, you want to count them only once per hospital admission. If the database contains age information at the time of admission, you want to use that information directly rather than calculating the age.
gold_sql: WITH FirstDepressionDiagnosis AS ( SELECT ad.patientid, ad.admissionid, ad.recordeddatetime AS first_diagnosis_time, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ad.patientid ORDER BY ad.recordeddatetime) AS rn FROM admissiondiagnoses ad JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion WHERE dc.description LIKE '%depressive disorder%' ), FirstDepressionAdmissions AS ( SELECT fdd.patientid, fdd.admissionid FROM FirstDepressionDiagnosis fdd JOIN hospitaladmissions ha ON fdd.admissionid = ha.admissionid WHERE ha.age BETWEEN 40 AND 59 AND fdd.rn = 1 ), UniqueMedications AS ( SELECT DISTINCT mo.admissionid, mo.patientid, mo.medicationname FROM medicationorders mo JOIN FirstDepressionAdmissions fda ON mo.admissionid = fda.admissionid ), MedicationCounts AS ( SELECT medicationname, COUNT(*) AS prescription_count, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rank FROM UniqueMedications GROUP BY medicationname ) SELECT medicationname FROM MedicationCounts WHERE rank <= 5 ORDER BY rank;

instruction: Your goal is to find data related to patient admissions. Specifically, you want to know the average age of patients admitted to the hospital. If the database contains the age at admission, you want to retrieve that information directly without calculating it. You want to limit the range of the final patient data to this month. If the database contains age information at the time of admission, you want to use that information directly rather than calculating the age.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(age), 4) AS average_age FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE datetime(admitdatetime, 'start of month') >= datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00', 'start of month');

instruction: Your goal is to find patients who underwent a specific test. Specifically, you want to identify patients diagnosed with diabetes in the past 180 days and determine how many times they did not have an HbA1c test recorded in the same hospital records. You want the diagnosis names that include the word "diabetes." You want to treat multiple records for the same patient as independent cases.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ad.admissionid) FROM admissiondiagnoses ad JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion WHERE dc.description LIKE '%diabetes%' AND datetime(ad.recordeddatetime) >= datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00','-180 days') AND ad.admissionid NOT IN ( SELECT lr.admissionid FROM labresults lr JOIN labtesttypes lt ON lr.itemcode = lt.itemcode WHERE lt.itemname = '% hemoglobin a1c' );

instruction: Your goal is to find information about a specific patient's procedures. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10021938 and you want to know how many times hemodialysis was performed in November this year.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS hemodialysis_count FROM admissionprocedures ap JOIN procedurecodes pc ON ap.icdcode = pc.icdcode AND ap.codeversion = pc.codeversion WHERE ap.patientid = 10021938 AND pc.description = 'hemodialysis' AND ap.recordeddatetime LIKE '2100-11-%';

instruction: Your goal is to find if a specific medication was ordered for patients. Specifically, you are interested in the list of patients prescribed apixaban. If prescription records exist, you want to know how many patients had a prescription start time within the last 90 days.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patientid) AS patient_count FROM medicationorders WHERE medicationname = 'apixaban' AND startdatetime >= datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00', '-90 days');

instruction: Your goal is to find the hospitalization details of a specific patient. Specifically, you want information on patient ID 10038933, and you want to know the time of admission through the emergency room.
gold_sql: SELECT hospitaladmissions.admitdatetime FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE hospitaladmissions.patientid = 10038933 AND hospitaladmissions.admitsource = 'emergency room';

instruction: Your goal is to find the most commonly prescribed medications for patients with a specific condition. Specifically, you want to know the top 5 medication names ordered during the same hospital admission as the alcohol abuse diagnosis. You want to search for diagnoses that include the word "alcohol abuse" in their names, but excludes family history of alcohol abuse. If multiple results tie for the same rank among the top frequent ranks, you want to retrieve all of them. If a patient has multiple records of alcohol abuse across hospital admissions, you only want the first alcohol abuse record among them. If a patient has multiple records of the same medication name, you want to count them only once per hospital admission.
gold_sql: WITH FirstAlcoholDiagnosis AS ( SELECT ad.patientid, ad.admissionid, ad.recordeddatetime AS first_alcohol_time, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ad.patientid ORDER BY ad.recordeddatetime) AS rn FROM admissiondiagnoses ad JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion WHERE dc.description LIKE '%alcohol abuse%' AND dc.description NOT LIKE '%family history%' ), FirstAlcoholPatients AS ( SELECT patientid, admissionid FROM FirstAlcoholDiagnosis WHERE rn = 1 ), UniquePrescriptions AS ( SELECT DISTINCT mo.admissionid, mo.patientid, mo.medicationname FROM medicationorders mo JOIN FirstAlcoholPatients fap ON mo.admissionid = fap.admissionid ), PrescriptionCounts AS ( SELECT medicationname AS drug, COUNT(*) AS prescription_count, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rank FROM UniquePrescriptions GROUP BY medicationname ) SELECT drug FROM PrescriptionCounts WHERE rank <= 5 ORDER BY rank;

instruction: Your goal is to find out if a patient had a specific diagnosis. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10036156 and you want to check if they have had any coagulation-related diagnoses so far. You want diagnosis names containing "coagulation." If such a diagnosis exists, you want to know the time of the first diagnosis.
gold_sql: SELECT ad.recordeddatetime FROM admissiondiagnoses ad JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion WHERE ad.patientid = 10036156 AND dc.description LIKE '%coagulation%' ORDER BY ad.recordeddatetime ASC LIMIT 1;

instruction: Your goal is to find cases where a patient was diagnosed with a specific condition and has a record of a specific medication being ordered. Specifically, you want to know how many hospital admissions there are where a patient was diagnosed with a urinary tract infection and, in the same hospital record, has a prescription record for ciprofloxacin after the diagnosis. You want diagnosis names containing "urinary tract infection." You want to treat multiple records for the same patient as independent cases.
gold_sql: WITH FirstDiagnosis AS ( SELECT ad.patientid, ad.admissionid, MIN(ad.recordeddatetime) AS first_diagnosis_time FROM admissiondiagnoses ad INNER JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion WHERE dc.description LIKE '%urinary tract infection%' GROUP BY ad.patientid, ad.admissionid ) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT FirstDiagnosis.admissionid) AS case_count FROM FirstDiagnosis INNER JOIN medicationorders mo ON FirstDiagnosis.admissionid = mo.admissionid WHERE mo.medicationname LIKE '%ciprofloxacin%' AND mo.startdatetime > FirstDiagnosis.first_diagnosis_time;

instruction: Your goal is to identify patients diagnosed with a specific condition. Specifically, you want to find the patient IDs of those diagnosed with tobacco use disorder. You want to search for diagnoses that include the term "tobacco use disorder" in their names, excluding those related to a personal history of tobacco use disorder. After obtaining the results, you want to narrow them down to diagnoses made within the last 180 days.
gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT hospitaladmissions.patientid FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE hospitaladmissions.admissionid IN ( SELECT admissiondiagnoses.admissionid FROM admissiondiagnoses JOIN diagnosiscodes ON admissiondiagnoses.icdcode = diagnosiscodes.icdcode AND admissiondiagnoses.codeversion = diagnosiscodes.codeversion WHERE diagnosiscodes.description LIKE '%tobacco use disorder%' AND diagnosiscodes.description NOT LIKE '%personal history%' AND datetime(admissiondiagnoses.recordeddatetime) >= datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00', '-180 days') );

instruction: Your goal is to find the number of patients who received a specific medication order after a particular procedure. Specifically, you want to know how many patients who underwent cardiac stent insertion had clopidogrel ordered during the same hospital admission. Since the database may record prescriptions before procedure, you want to focus on prescriptions within the same hospital admission as the procedure.
gold_sql: WITH StentProcedures AS ( SELECT ap.patientid, ap.admissionid, ap.recordeddatetime FROM admissionprocedures ap JOIN procedurecodes pc ON ap.icdcode = pc.icdcode AND ap.codeversion = pc.codeversion WHERE pc.description IN ( 'insertion of one vascular stent', 'insertion of drug-eluting coronary artery stent(s)' ) ), ClopidogrelPrescriptions AS ( SELECT mo.patientid, mo.admissionid, mo.startdatetime FROM medicationorders mo WHERE mo.medicationname = 'clopidogrel' ), StentThenClopidogrel AS ( SELECT DISTINCT sp.patientid FROM StentProcedures sp JOIN ClopidogrelPrescriptions cp ON sp.admissionid = cp.admissionid ) SELECT COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM StentThenClopidogrel;

instruction: Your goal is to find information related to a specific patient's medication orders. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10004235 and you want to know the top three most frequently prescribed medications from their last hospital visit. If multiple results tie for the same rank among the top frequent ranks, you want to retrieve all of them.
gold_sql: WITH LastAdmission AS ( SELECT admissionid FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE patientid = 10004235 ORDER BY admitdatetime DESC LIMIT 1 ), DrugCounts AS ( SELECT mo.medicationname AS drug, COUNT(*) AS prescription_count, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rank FROM medicationorders mo INNER JOIN LastAdmission la ON mo.admissionid = la.admissionid GROUP BY mo.medicationname ) SELECT drug FROM DrugCounts WHERE rank <= 3 ORDER BY rank;

instruction: Your goal is to find information related to hospital patient discharges. Specifically, you want to count the number of unique patients with discharge records, and you want the results limited to records after 1 PM yesterday.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT hospitaladmissions.patientid) FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE hospitaladmissions.dischargedatetime IS NOT NULL AND datetime(hospitaladmissions.dischargedatetime) > datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00', '-1 day', 'start of day', '+13 hours');

instruction: Your goal is to find lab test information related to patients with a specific diagnosis. Specifically, you are interested in patients diagnosed with acute alcoholic hepatitis, and you want to know the top three most frequently performed lab test names in the same hospital record. If multiple results tie for the same rank among the top frequent ranks, you want to retrieve all of them. If a patient has multiple records of acute alcoholic hepatitis across hospital admissions, you only want the first acute alcoholic hepatitis record among them. If a patient has multiple records of the same lab test name, you want to count them only once per hospital admission.
gold_sql: WITH FirstHepatitisDiagnosis AS ( SELECT ad.patientid, ad.admissionid, ad.recordeddatetime AS first_hepatitis_time, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ad.patientid ORDER BY ad.recordeddatetime) AS rn FROM admissiondiagnoses ad JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion WHERE dc.description = 'acute alcoholic hepatitis' ), FirstHepatitisPatients AS ( SELECT patientid, admissionid FROM FirstHepatitisDiagnosis WHERE rn = 1 ), UniqueLabTests AS ( SELECT DISTINCT lr.admissionid, lr.patientid, lt.itemname AS lab_test_name FROM labresults lr JOIN labtesttypes lt ON lr.itemcode = lt.itemcode JOIN FirstHepatitisPatients fhp ON lr.admissionid = fhp.admissionid ), LabTestCounts AS ( SELECT lab_test_name, COUNT(*) AS test_count, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rank FROM UniqueLabTests GROUP BY lab_test_name ) SELECT lab_test_name FROM LabTestCounts WHERE rank <= 3 ORDER BY rank;

instruction: Your goal is to find information about patients who received a diagnosis. Specifically, you want to know the number of unique patients who had a diagnosis associated with a highway accident. You want the diagnosis names that include the word "highway."
gold_sql: WITH HighwayDiagnoses AS ( SELECT DISTINCT ad.patientid FROM admissiondiagnoses ad JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion WHERE dc.description LIKE '%highway%' ) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patientid) AS unique_patient_count FROM HighwayDiagnoses;

instruction: Your goal is to find information about patient hospitalization records. Specifically, you want to know the number of patients currently hospitalized with an admission duration of seven days or longer. You want to count the unique number of patients.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patientid) AS long_stay_patient_count FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE dischargedatetime IS NULL AND julianday('2100-12-31 23:59:00') - julianday(admitdatetime) >= 7;

instruction: Your goal is to find statistics on patients with a specific diagnosis. Specifically, you want to know how many patients were first diagnosed with cirrhosis and died in the same month. You want diagnosis names containing "cirrhosis."
gold_sql: WITH CirrhosisDiagnoses AS ( SELECT ad.patientid, ad.admissionid, ad.recordeddatetime FROM admissiondiagnoses ad JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion WHERE dc.description LIKE '%cirrhosis%' ), FirstCirrhosis AS ( SELECT patientid, MIN(recordeddatetime) AS first_recordeddatetime FROM CirrhosisDiagnoses GROUP BY patientid ), DeathInSameMonth AS ( SELECT DISTINCT fc.patientid FROM FirstCirrhosis fc JOIN demographics d ON fc.patientid = d.patientid WHERE d.dateofdeath IS NOT NULL AND strftime('%Y-%m', fc.first_recordeddatetime) = strftime('%Y-%m', d.dateofdeath) ) SELECT COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM DeathInSameMonth;

instruction: Your goal is to find statistics related to patient admissions. Specifically, you want to focus on which four-hour time period (e.g., 00:00 - 03:59, 04:00 - 07:59, etc.), out of the six daily periods, has the highest number of admission records through the emergency room. You want to request the DB agent to format the output as '00:00 - 00:00' using SQL.
gold_sql: WITH ERAdmissions AS ( SELECT admitdatetime FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE admitsource = 'emergency room' ), TimeSlots AS ( SELECT CASE WHEN CAST(strftime('%H', admitdatetime) AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 0 AND 3 THEN '00:00 - 03:59' WHEN CAST(strftime('%H', admitdatetime) AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 4 AND 7 THEN '04:00 - 07:59' WHEN CAST(strftime('%H', admitdatetime) AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 8 AND 11 THEN '08:00 - 11:59' WHEN CAST(strftime('%H', admitdatetime) AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 12 AND 15 THEN '12:00 - 15:59' WHEN CAST(strftime('%H', admitdatetime) AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 16 AND 19 THEN '16:00 - 19:59' ELSE '20:00 - 23:59' END AS time_slot, COUNT(*) AS admission_count FROM ERAdmissions GROUP BY time_slot ), MaxAdmissions AS ( SELECT MAX(admission_count) AS max_count FROM TimeSlots ) SELECT ts.time_slot FROM TimeSlots ts JOIN MaxAdmissions ma ON ts.admission_count = ma.max_count ORDER BY ts.time_slot;

instruction: Your goal is to find statistics related to lab tests. Specifically, you want to know the percentage of total lab test cases accounted for by the five most frequently performed lab tests, all combined. If multiple results tie for the same rank among the top frequent ranks, you want to retrieve all of them. You want to request these results first and then limit the final results to lab tests conducted over the past 180 days. You want the result in percentage (%).
gold_sql: WITH LabCounts AS ( SELECT lt.itemname AS test_label, COUNT(*) AS test_count, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rank FROM labresults lr JOIN labtesttypes lt ON lr.itemcode = lt.itemcode WHERE datetime(lr.resultdatetime) >= datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00','-180 days') GROUP BY test_label ), TopTests AS ( SELECT SUM(test_count) AS top_test_count FROM LabCounts WHERE rank <= 5 ), TotalTests AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_test_count FROM labresults WHERE datetime(resultdatetime) >= datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00','-180 days') ) SELECT ROUND(100.0 * tt.top_test_count / t.total_test_count, 4) AS percentage FROM TopTests tt, TotalTests t;

instruction: Your goal is to find prescription-related cost information. Specifically, you want to know the total cost of the five most frequently ordered medications for patients this year. If multiple results tie for the same rank among the top frequent ranks, you want to retrieve all of them. You want the total cost, not the amount spent on each medication.
gold_sql: WITH drug_counts AS ( SELECT medicationname AS drug, COUNT(*) AS prescription_count, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rank FROM medicationorders WHERE strftime('%Y', startdatetime) = '2100' GROUP BY medicationname ), top_drugs AS ( SELECT drug FROM drug_counts WHERE rank <= 5 ) SELECT ROUND(SUM(cr.costamount), 4) AS total_cost FROM costrecords cr JOIN medicationorders mo ON cr.costid = mo.recordid AND cr.eventtype = 'medicationorders' JOIN top_drugs td ON mo.medicationname = td.drug WHERE strftime('%Y', mo.startdatetime) = '2100'

instruction: Your goal is to find the medications prescribed to a patient. You are interested in patient ID 10001725 and you want to know all medications ordered within the same hospital admission record following an anaphylactic reaction diagnosis during a hospital visit in April this year. You want diagnosis names containing "anaphylactic."
gold_sql: WITH anaphylactic_codes AS ( SELECT icdcode, codeversion FROM diagnosiscodes WHERE description LIKE '%anaphylactic%' ), admission_ids AS ( SELECT admissionid FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE patientid = 10001725 AND strftime('%Y-%m', admitdatetime) = '2100-04' ), anaphylactic_admissions AS ( SELECT a.admissionid, d.recordeddatetime FROM admission_ids a JOIN admissiondiagnoses d ON a.admissionid = d.admissionid JOIN anaphylactic_codes ac ON d.icdcode = ac.icdcode AND d.codeversion = ac.codeversion ) SELECT DISTINCT m.medicationname FROM medicationorders m JOIN anaphylactic_admissions aa ON m.admissionid = aa.admissionid WHERE m.startdatetime >= aa.recordeddatetime;

instruction: Your goal is to find statistics related to lab tests. Specifically, you want to identify the top five lab tests. If multiple results tie for the same rank among the top frequent ranks, you want to retrieve all of them. You want the results first and ultimately want to limit the results to lab tests conducted over the past 180 days.
gold_sql: WITH LabCounts AS ( SELECT lt.itemname AS test_label, COUNT(*) AS test_count, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rank FROM labresults lr JOIN labtesttypes lt ON lr.itemcode = lt.itemcode WHERE lr.resultdatetime >= datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00', '-180 days') GROUP BY lower(lt.itemname) ) SELECT test_label FROM LabCounts WHERE rank <= 5 ORDER BY rank;

instruction: Your goal is to find statistics related to patient input events. Specifically, you want to know the average hospital stay for patients with vasopressin administration records, but only those whose average daily dose was at least 20% higher than the average daily dose for all vasopressin-administered patients during a single hospital stay. You want to include only patients with discharge records and exclude those who died. You want to treat multiple records for the same patient as independent cases. You want the vasopressin data from patient input records, not prescription records.
gold_sql: WITH VasopressinAdmin AS ( SELECT i.patientid, i.admissionid, date(i.startdatetime) AS admin_date, SUM(i.totalvolume) AS daily_amount FROM intakerecords i JOIN clinicalitemtypes d ON i.itemcode = d.itemcode WHERE d.itemname = 'vasopressin' AND i.totalvolume IS NOT NULL AND i.totalvolume > 0 GROUP BY i.patientid, i.admissionid, admin_date ), PatientAvgDaily AS ( SELECT patientid, admissionid, AVG(daily_amount) AS patient_avg_daily FROM VasopressinAdmin GROUP BY patientid, admissionid ), HospitalAvgDaily AS ( SELECT AVG(daily_amount) AS hospital_avg_daily FROM VasopressinAdmin ), HighDosePatients AS ( SELECT DISTINCT pad.patientid, pad.admissionid FROM PatientAvgDaily pad JOIN hospitaladmissions a ON pad.admissionid = a.admissionid JOIN demographics p ON pad.patientid = p.patientid WHERE a.dischargedatetime IS NOT NULL AND p.dateofdeath IS NULL AND pad.patient_avg_daily >= (SELECT hospital_avg_daily FROM HospitalAvgDaily) * 1.2 ) SELECT ROUND(AVG(JULIANDAY(a.dischargedatetime) - JULIANDAY(a.admitdatetime)), 4) AS avg_stay_days FROM HighDosePatients hdp JOIN hospitaladmissions a ON hdp.admissionid = a.admissionid;

instruction: Your goal is to find the patient's diagnostic record. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10018845 and you want to know the list of diagnoses recorded during their first hospital visit.
gold_sql: WITH FirstAdmission AS ( SELECT admissionid FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE patientid = 10018845 ORDER BY admitdatetime LIMIT 1 ) SELECT dc.description FROM admissiondiagnoses ad JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion JOIN FirstAdmission fa ON ad.admissionid = fa.admissionid WHERE ad.patientid = 10018845;
gold_answer: subdural hemorrhage following injury without mention of open intracranial wound, unspecified state of consciousness
coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage v or end stage renal disease

instruction: Your goal is to find information related to the patient care unit. You are interested in patient ID 10039831 and want to know how many hours the patient has stayed in the surgical intensive care unit since being transferred there until now. You want the duration to be calculated in hours.
gold_sql: WITH SurgicalICUTransfer AS ( SELECT pt.transferindatetime AS intime, pt.transferoutdatetime AS outtime FROM patienttransfers pt WHERE pt.patientid = 10039831 AND pt.careunit = 'surgical intensive care unit (sicu)' AND pt.transferindatetime IS NOT NULL ORDER BY pt.transferindatetime DESC LIMIT 1 ) SELECT ROUND(24 * (JULIANDAY(COALESCE(s.outtime, '2100-12-31 23:59:00')) - JULIANDAY(s.intime)), 4) AS hours_in_sicu FROM SurgicalICUTransfer s;

instruction: Your goal is to find the most common diagnoses among patients of a specific age group. Specifically, you want to identify the top five most common diagnoses for middle-aged patients. You want to define middle-aged patients as those aged 45 to 64 years. If multiple results tie for the same rank among the top frequent ranks, you want to retrieve all of them. If the database contains age information at the time of admission, you want to use that information directly rather than calculating the age.
gold_sql: WITH MiddleAgeDiagnoses AS ( SELECT dc.description AS diagnosis, COUNT(*) AS diagnosis_count, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rank FROM admissiondiagnoses ad JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion JOIN hospitaladmissions ha ON ad.admissionid = ha.admissionid WHERE ha.age BETWEEN 45 AND 64 GROUP BY diagnosis ) SELECT diagnosis FROM MiddleAgeDiagnoses WHERE rank <= 5 ORDER BY rank;
gold_answer: diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type ii or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled

instruction: Your goal is to find information about patients' output records. Specifically, you want the admissionid of patients who had a daily I/O of +500 or more at least once this month.
gold_sql: WITH DailyInput AS ( SELECT i.admissionid, DATE(i.startdatetime) AS event_date, SUM(i.totalvolume) AS total_input FROM intakerecords i WHERE datetime(i.startdatetime, 'start of month') = datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00', 'start of month') AND i.volumeunit = 'ml' GROUP BY i.admissionid, DATE(i.startdatetime) ), DailyOutput AS ( SELECT o.admissionid, DATE(o.recordeddatetime) AS event_date, SUM(o.volume) AS total_output FROM outputrecords o WHERE datetime(o.recordeddatetime, 'start of month') = datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00', 'start of month') AND o.volumeunit = 'ml' GROUP BY o.admissionid, DATE(o.recordeddatetime) ), AllDates AS ( SELECT admissionid, event_date FROM DailyInput UNION SELECT admissionid, event_date FROM DailyOutput ), DailyIO AS ( SELECT d.admissionid, COALESCE(( SELECT total_input FROM DailyInput i WHERE i.admissionid = d.admissionid AND i.event_date = d.event_date ), 0) - COALESCE(( SELECT total_output FROM DailyOutput o WHERE o.admissionid = d.admissionid AND o.event_date = d.event_date ), 0) AS net_io FROM AllDates d WHERE COALESCE(( SELECT total_input FROM DailyInput i WHERE i.admissionid = d.admissionid AND i.event_date = d.event_date ), 0) - COALESCE(( SELECT total_output FROM DailyOutput o WHERE o.admissionid = d.admissionid AND o.event_date = d.event_date ), 0) >= 500 ) SELECT DISTINCT admissionid FROM DailyIO ORDER BY admissionid;

instruction: Your goal is to find information related to a patient’s prescription history. Specifically, you want to know the total volume of vancomycin ordered for patient ID 10004235, who was diagnosed with acute kidney failure, during the five days following the diagnosis in March of this year. You want diagnosis names containing "acute kidney failure."
gold_sql: WITH kidney_failure_codes AS ( SELECT icdcode, codeversion FROM diagnosiscodes WHERE description LIKE '%acute kidney failure%' ), admission_ids AS ( SELECT admissionid FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE patientid = 10004235 AND admitdatetime LIKE '2100-03%' ), kidney_failure_admissions AS ( SELECT a.admissionid, d.recordeddatetime FROM admission_ids a JOIN admissiondiagnoses d ON a.admissionid = d.admissionid JOIN kidney_failure_codes kfc ON d.icdcode = kfc.icdcode AND d.codeversion = kfc.codeversion ) SELECT COALESCE(SUM(CAST(m.dosevalue AS REAL)), 0) AS total_dose FROM medicationorders m JOIN kidney_failure_admissions kfa ON m.admissionid = kfa.admissionid WHERE m.medicationname LIKE '%vancomycin%' AND datetime(m.startdatetime) BETWEEN datetime(kfa.recordeddatetime) AND datetime(kfa.recordeddatetime, '+5 days');

instruction: Your goal is to find information related to patient lab tests. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10022017 and you want to know which lab tests were performed on the day of hospital discharge in October this year. You are referring to the discharge date, not the discharge time.
gold_sql: WITH DischargeAdmissions AS ( SELECT admissionid, date(dischargedatetime) AS discharge_date FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE patientid = 10022017 AND dischargedatetime LIKE '2100-10%' AND dischargedatetime IS NOT NULL ) SELECT DISTINCT lt.itemname AS test_label FROM labresults lr JOIN labtesttypes lt ON lr.itemcode = lt.itemcode JOIN DischargeAdmissions da ON lr.admissionid = da.admissionid WHERE lr.patientid = 10022017 AND date(lr.resultdatetime) = da.discharge_date ORDER BY test_label;

instruction: Your goal is to find statistics related to patient input events and hospital stays. Specifically, you want to identify the average hospital stay duration for patients who have at least one record of morphine administration three or more times within 24 hours. You want the average hospital stay duration in days. You want the morphine data from patient input records, not prescription records.
gold_sql: WITH morphine_admin AS ( SELECT i.patientid, i.admissionid, i.startdatetime FROM intakerecords i JOIN clinicalitemtypes d ON i.itemcode = d.itemcode WHERE lower(d.itemname) LIKE '%morphine%' ), frequent_admin AS ( SELECT DISTINCT ma1.patientid, ma1.admissionid FROM morphine_admin ma1 WHERE EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM morphine_admin ma2 WHERE ma2.patientid = ma1.patientid AND datetime(ma1.startdatetime) BETWEEN datetime(ma2.startdatetime) AND datetime(ma2.startdatetime, '+24 hours') GROUP BY ma2.patientid, ma2.admissionid HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 ) ) SELECT ROUND(AVG(JULIANDAY(a.dischargedatetime) - JULIANDAY(a.admitdatetime)), 4) AS avg_stay_days FROM hospitaladmissions a JOIN frequent_admin fa ON a.patientid = fa.patientid AND a.admissionid = fa.admissionid WHERE a.dischargedatetime IS NOT NULL;

instruction: Your goal is to find if a specific type of microbiological test was performed on a patient. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10037975 and want to know if a respiratory culture test was conducted. If such a test was performed, request information on which bacteria were identified.
gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT organismname FROM microbiologyresults WHERE patientid = 10037975 AND testname = 'respiratory culture';

instruction: Your goal is to find information about lab tests performed after a specific surgery. You are interested in CABG and want to know the top five most commonly performed lab tests during the same hospital admission. Since the database may record lab tests from before surgery, you want to focus on tests within the same hospital admission as the surgery. If multiple results tie for the same rank among the top frequent ranks, you want to retrieve all of them. If a patient has multiple records of CABG across hospital admissions, you only want the first CABG record among them. If a patient has multiple records of the same lab test name, you want to count them only once per hospital admission.
gold_sql: WITH FirstCABGProcedure AS ( SELECT ap.patientid, ap.admissionid, ap.recordeddatetime AS first_cabg_time, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ap.patientid ORDER BY ap.recordeddatetime) AS rn FROM admissionprocedures ap JOIN procedurecodes pc ON ap.icdcode = pc.icdcode AND ap.codeversion = pc.codeversion WHERE pc.description IN ( 'single internal mammary-coronary artery bypass', '(aorto)coronary bypass of four or more coronary arteries', '(aorto)coronary bypass of two coronary arteries', 'bypass coronary artery, one artery from left internal mammary, open approach', 'bypass coronary artery, one artery from left internal mammary with autologous arterial tissue, open approach', 'bypass coronary artery, one artery from aorta with autologous venous tissue, open approach', 'bypass coronary artery, one artery from right internal mammary with autologous arterial tissue, open approach', 'bypass coronary artery, three arteries from aorta with autologous venous tissue, open approach', '(aorto)coronary bypass of three coronary arteries' ) ), FirstCABGAdmissions AS ( SELECT patientid, admissionid FROM FirstCABGProcedure WHERE rn = 1 ), UniqueLabTests AS ( SELECT DISTINCT lr.admissionid, lr.patientid, lt.itemname AS lab_test_name FROM labresults lr JOIN labtesttypes lt ON lr.itemcode = lt.itemcode JOIN FirstCABGAdmissions fca ON lr.admissionid = fca.admissionid ), LabTestCounts AS ( SELECT lab_test_name, COUNT(*) AS test_count, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rank FROM UniqueLabTests GROUP BY lab_test_name ) SELECT lab_test_name FROM LabTestCounts WHERE rank <= 5 ORDER BY rank;

instruction: Your goal is to find cost-related information for a specific patient. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10000032 and you want to know the average total cost incurred from each hospital admission for this patient.
gold_sql: WITH PerAdmissionCost AS ( SELECT ha.admissionid, SUM(cr.costamount) AS total_cost FROM hospitaladmissions ha JOIN costrecords cr ON ha.admissionid = cr.admissionid WHERE ha.patientid = 10000032 GROUP BY ha.admissionid ) SELECT ROUND(AVG(total_cost), 4) AS average_cost FROM PerAdmissionCost;

instruction: Your goal is to find statistics related to patient hospitalizations. Specifically, you want to know the top three locations where patients have been admitted to the hospital. If multiple results tie for the same rank among the top frequent ranks, you want to retrieve all of them. Once you obtain the results, you want to narrow down the result to those for patients admitted this month.
gold_sql: WITH RankedSources AS ( SELECT ha.admitsource, COUNT(*) as admission_count, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) as rank FROM hospitaladmissions ha WHERE datetime(ha.admitdatetime, 'start of month') = datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00', 'start of month') GROUP BY ha.admitsource ) SELECT admitsource FROM RankedSources WHERE rank <= 3 ORDER BY rank;

instruction: Your goal is to find vital sign information for a specific patient. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10001725 and want to know the exact times during their last hospital admission when their heart rate increased by 20 bpm or more within a 10-minute period.
gold_sql: WITH PatientVitals AS ( SELECT ce.admissionid, ce.recordeddatetime, ce.value AS heart_rate, ha.patientid FROM clinicalevents ce JOIN clinicalitemtypes cit ON ce.itemcode = cit.itemcode JOIN hospitaladmissions ha ON ce.admissionid = ha.admissionid WHERE cit.itemname = 'heart rate' AND ha.patientid = 10001725 AND ce.value IS NOT NULL AND ce.recordeddatetime >= ha.admitdatetime AND (ce.recordeddatetime <= ha.dischargedatetime OR ha.dischargedatetime IS NULL) AND ce.admissionid = ( SELECT admissionid FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE patientid = 10001725 ORDER BY admitdatetime DESC LIMIT 1 ) ), VitalChanges AS ( SELECT v1.recordeddatetime AS start_time, v2.recordeddatetime AS end_time, v2.heart_rate - v1.heart_rate AS hr_change FROM PatientVitals v1 JOIN PatientVitals v2 ON v1.admissionid = v2.admissionid WHERE datetime(v2.recordeddatetime) BETWEEN datetime(v1.recordeddatetime) AND datetime(v1.recordeddatetime, '+10 minutes') ) SELECT end_time FROM VitalChanges WHERE hr_change >= 20 ORDER BY end_time;

instruction: Your goal is to find the total number of cases for a specific procedure. Specifically, you want to know how many EVD insertions have been performed to date. You want to retrieve the results and then narrow them down to the total number of cases performed this month.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM admissionprocedures WHERE (admissionprocedures.icdcode, admissionprocedures.codeversion) IN ( SELECT pc.icdcode, pc.codeversion FROM procedurecodes pc WHERE pc.description = 'insertion or replacement of external ventricular drain [evd]' ) AND datetime(admissionprocedures.recordeddatetime, 'start of month') = datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00', 'start of month');

instruction: Your goal is to find information related to a patient’s intake record. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10004733 and you want to know the most recent intake administration time from yesterday. You want the data from patient input records, not prescription records.
gold_sql: SELECT MAX(startdatetime) AS last_intake_time FROM intakerecords WHERE patientid = 10004733 AND datetime(startdatetime, 'start of day') = datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00', 'start of day', '-1 day');

instruction: Your goal is to find information related to patient input events. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10004733 and you want to know the last administration time of norepinephrine during this hospital admission. You want the actual administration time, not the order start time. You want the norepinephrine data from patient input records, not prescription records.
gold_sql: WITH latest_admission AS ( SELECT admissionid FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE patientid = 10004733 AND dischargedatetime IS NULL ORDER BY admitdatetime DESC LIMIT 1 ) SELECT MAX(ir.startdatetime) AS last_administration_time FROM intakerecords ir JOIN clinicalitemtypes cit ON ir.itemcode = cit.itemcode JOIN latest_admission la ON ir.admissionid = la.admissionid WHERE ir.patientid = 10004733 AND cit.itemname LIKE '%norepinephrine%';

instruction: Your goal is to find emergency room-related statistics. Specifically, you want to know the top five diagnoses received by patients admitted through the emergency room. If multiple results tie for the same rank among the top frequent ranks, you want to retrieve all of them. You want to count each admission through the emergency room independently, even if a patient was admitted multiple times. If a patient has multiple records of the same diagnosis name, you want to count them only once per hospital admission.
gold_sql: WITH er_admissions AS ( SELECT admissionid FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE admitsource = 'emergency room' ), deduped_diags AS ( SELECT DISTINCT ad.admissionid, ad.icdcode, ad.codeversion FROM admissiondiagnoses ad JOIN er_admissions ea ON ad.admissionid = ea.admissionid ), diag_counts AS ( SELECT dc.description, COUNT(*) as diag_count FROM deduped_diags dd JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON dd.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND dd.codeversion = dc.codeversion GROUP BY dc.description ), ranked_diags AS ( SELECT description, diag_count, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY diag_count DESC) as rank FROM diag_counts ) SELECT description FROM ranked_diags WHERE rank <= 5 ORDER BY rank;
gold_answer: diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type ii or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
urinary tract infection, site not specified

instruction: Your goal is to find medication information related to a patient’s prescription. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10025463, and you want to know which medications were recorded as starting on the hospital discharge date in November of this year. You are referring to the discharge date, not the discharge time.
gold_sql: WITH PatientAdmission AS ( SELECT admissionid, dischargedatetime, date(dischargedatetime) AS discharge_date FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE patientid = 10025463 AND dischargedatetime LIKE '2100-11%' ORDER BY dischargedatetime DESC LIMIT 1 ) SELECT DISTINCT m.medicationname FROM medicationorders m WHERE m.admissionid IN (SELECT admissionid FROM PatientAdmission) AND date(m.startdatetime) = (SELECT discharge_date FROM PatientAdmission)

instruction: Your goal is to find statistics on patient procedures. Specifically, you want to identify the top five procedures performed on patients within 90 days after undergoing percutaneous abdominal drainage. You want to search for percutaneous abdominal drainage specifically, not other similar procedures. When querying the DB agent, since you do not know how percutaneous abdominal drainage is stored, use common terms like "PAD" when referring to it, and let the DB agent find it for you. If multiple results tie for the same rank among the top frequent ranks, you want to retrieve all of them. If a patient has multiple records of PAD across hospital admissions, you only want the first PAD record among them, and subsequent other procedures counted only once per patient.
gold_sql: WITH FirstPADProcedures AS ( SELECT ap.patientid, ap.admissionid, ap.recordeddatetime AS pad_time, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ap.patientid ORDER BY ap.recordeddatetime) AS rn FROM admissionprocedures ap JOIN procedurecodes pc ON ap.icdcode = pc.icdcode AND ap.codeversion = pc.codeversion WHERE pc.description = 'percutaneous abdominal drainage' ), FirstPAD AS ( SELECT patientid, admissionid, pad_time FROM FirstPADProcedures WHERE rn = 1 ), OtherProcedures AS ( SELECT DISTINCT fp.patientid, pc.description AS procedure_name FROM admissionprocedures ap JOIN procedurecodes pc ON ap.icdcode = pc.icdcode AND ap.codeversion = pc.codeversion JOIN FirstPAD fp ON ap.patientid = fp.patientid WHERE pc.description != 'percutaneous abdominal drainage' AND datetime(ap.recordeddatetime) BETWEEN datetime(fp.pad_time) AND datetime(fp.pad_time, '+90 days') ), ProcedureCounts AS ( SELECT procedure_name, COUNT(*) AS procedure_count, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rank FROM OtherProcedures GROUP BY procedure_name ) SELECT procedure_name FROM ProcedureCounts WHERE rank <= 5 ORDER BY rank;
gold_answer: enteral infusion of concentrated nutritional substances
other excision or destruction of lesion or tissue of pancreas or pancreatic duct
drainage of pancreatic cyst by catheter
diagnostic ultrasound of abdomen and retroperitoneum
control of epistaxis by anterior nasal packing
continuous invasive mechanical ventilation for less than 96 consecutive hours

instruction: Your goal is to find the medications ordered alongside a specific drug. Specifically, you want to know the top five most frequently prescribed medications for patients within 30 days after receiving ciprofloxacin-containing medications. Count all instances of each medication, even if prescribed multiple times to the same patient. If multiple results tie for the same rank among the top frequent ranks, you want to retrieve all of them. You want medications containing ciprofloxacin excluded from the final medications list.
gold_sql: WITH cipro_medicationorders AS ( SELECT patientid, admissionid, startdatetime FROM medicationorders WHERE medicationname LIKE '%ciprofloxacin%' ), related_medicationorders AS ( SELECT mo.medicationname FROM medicationorders mo JOIN cipro_medicationorders cmo ON mo.patientid = cmo.patientid AND datetime(mo.startdatetime) BETWEEN datetime(cmo.startdatetime) AND datetime(cmo.startdatetime, '+30 days') WHERE mo.medicationname NOT LIKE '%ciprofloxacin%' ), medication_counts AS ( SELECT medicationname, COUNT(*) as prescription_count, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) as rank FROM related_medicationorders GROUP BY medicationname ) SELECT medicationname FROM medication_counts WHERE rank <= 5 ORDER BY rank;

instruction: Your goal is to find information related to a specific patient’s vital signs over time. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10021487 and you want to know the last time during this hospital admission when the mean BP was 65mmHg or lower.
gold_sql: WITH LastAdmission AS ( SELECT admissionid, admitdatetime FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE patientid = 10021487 AND dischargedatetime IS NULL ORDER BY admitdatetime DESC LIMIT 1 ), MeanBPEvents AS ( SELECT ce.recordeddatetime, ce.value AS mean_bp, ce.unit FROM clinicalevents ce JOIN clinicalitemtypes cit ON ce.itemcode = cit.itemcode JOIN LastAdmission la ON ce.admissionid = la.admissionid WHERE ce.patientid = 10021487 AND cit.itemname = 'arterial blood pressure mean' AND ce.value IS NOT NULL AND ce.value <= 65 ) SELECT recordeddatetime AS last_mean_bp_below_65 FROM MeanBPEvents ORDER BY recordeddatetime DESC LIMIT 1;

instruction: Your goal is to find patient information. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10015860 and you want to know the patient’s gender.
gold_sql: SELECT demographics.gender FROM demographics WHERE demographics.patientid = 10015860;

instruction: Your goal is to find the Net I&O information for a patient. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10004733 and you want to know the daily Net I/O for the current hospitalization period. You want the final value to be calculated as the daily input amount minus the output amount.
gold_sql: WITH CurrentAdmission AS ( SELECT admissionid FROM hospitaladmissions WHERE patientid = 10004733 AND (dischargedatetime IS NULL OR dischargedatetime = '') ORDER BY admitdatetime DESC LIMIT 1 ), DailyInput AS ( SELECT DATE(i.startdatetime) AS event_date, SUM(i.totalvolume) AS total_input FROM intakerecords i INNER JOIN CurrentAdmission ca ON i.admissionid = ca.admissionid WHERE i.patientid = 10004733 GROUP BY DATE(i.startdatetime) ), DailyOutput AS ( SELECT DATE(o.recordeddatetime) AS event_date, SUM(o.volume) AS total_output FROM outputrecords o INNER JOIN CurrentAdmission ca ON o.admissionid = ca.admissionid WHERE o.patientid = 10004733 GROUP BY DATE(o.recordeddatetime) ), AllDates AS ( SELECT event_date FROM DailyInput UNION SELECT event_date FROM DailyOutput ) SELECT COALESCE(( SELECT total_input FROM DailyInput i WHERE i.event_date = d.event_date ), 0) - COALESCE(( SELECT total_output FROM DailyOutput o WHERE o.event_date = d.event_date ), 0) AS net_io FROM AllDates d ORDER BY d.event_date;

instruction: Your goal is to find the cost associated with a lab test. Specifically, you want to know the cost of a single BUN (blood urea nitrogen) test. You are looking for the lab test named "urea nitrogen" (where "blood" may be omitted), but you do not want lab tests that include other specimen types such as urine or body fluid in their names.
gold_sql: WITH UreaNitrogenLabItems AS ( SELECT itemcode FROM labtesttypes WHERE itemname = 'urea nitrogen' ), UreaNitrogenLabResults AS ( SELECT recordid FROM labresults WHERE itemcode IN ( SELECT itemcode FROM UreaNitrogenLabItems ) ), UreaNitrogenCosts AS ( SELECT DISTINCT costamount FROM costrecords WHERE eventtype = 'labresults' AND costid IN ( SELECT recordid FROM UreaNitrogenLabResults ) ) SELECT costamount FROM UreaNitrogenCosts;

instruction: Your goal is to find information related to input events. Specifically, you want to know, for patients diagnosed with myocardial infarction, if they had heparin and nitroglycerin administered on the same day. You want to calculate the daily average of the total dose administered for each drug. You want the average values presented in alphabetical order: heparin first, then nitroglycerin. You want each medication and its variants to be treated as a single medication (e.g., heparin sodium and heparin sodium (impella) are both considered heparin). You want diagnosis names containing "myocardial infarction." You want the heparin and nitroglycerin data from patient input records, not prescription records.
gold_sql: WITH MI_Patients AS ( SELECT DISTINCT ad.patientid FROM admissiondiagnoses ad JOIN diagnosiscodes dc ON ad.icdcode = dc.icdcode AND ad.codeversion = dc.codeversion WHERE lower(dc.description) LIKE '%myocardial infarction%' ), DrugAdmin AS ( SELECT ir.patientid, CASE WHEN LOWER(cit.itemname) LIKE '%heparin%' THEN 'heparin' WHEN LOWER(cit.itemname) LIKE '%nitroglycerin%' THEN 'nitroglycerin' ELSE NULL END AS drug, DATE(ir.startdatetime) AS admin_date, ir.totalvolume AS volume_ml FROM intakerecords ir JOIN clinicalitemtypes cit ON ir.itemcode = cit.itemcode JOIN MI_Patients mp ON ir.patientid = mp.patientid WHERE drug IS NOT NULL ), SameDayFluids AS ( SELECT patientid, admin_date FROM DrugAdmin GROUP BY patientid, admin_date HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT drug) = 2 ), DailyTotals AS ( SELECT ad.drug, ad.admin_date, SUM(ad.volume_ml) AS daily_total_volume FROM DrugAdmin ad JOIN SameDayFluids sdf ON ad.patientid = sdf.patientid AND ad.admin_date = sdf.admin_date GROUP BY drug, ad.admin_date ) SELECT ROUND(AVG(daily_total_volume), 4) AS average_daily_dose FROM DailyTotals GROUP BY drug ORDER BY drug ASC;

instruction: Your goal is to determine whether a specific lab test was performed for a particular patient. Specifically, you want to check if patient ID 10031757 underwent an ALT test. If the test was performed, ask to indicate the time of the most recent test.
gold_sql: SELECT lr.resultdatetime FROM labresults lr JOIN labtesttypes lt ON lr.itemcode = lt.itemcode WHERE lr.patientid = 10031757 AND lt.itemname = 'alanine aminotransferase (alt)' ORDER BY lr.resultdatetime DESC LIMIT 1;

instruction: Your goal is to find statistics related to medical procedures. Specifically, you want to know the total number of patients who underwent a spinal tap. You want to order the results initially, and ultimately, you want the results limited to patients who underwent the procedure in the last 180 days.
gold_sql: WITH SpinalTapProcedures AS ( SELECT DISTINCT ap.patientid FROM admissionprocedures ap JOIN procedurecodes pc ON ap.icdcode = pc.icdcode AND ap.codeversion = pc.codeversion WHERE pc.description = 'spinal tap' AND datetime(ap.recordeddatetime) >= datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00','-180 days') ) SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_patients FROM SpinalTapProcedures;

instruction: Your goal is to find information about patient admissions and discharges. Specifically, you are interested in patient ID 10000032 and you want to know the discharge times for this patient.
